answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent, setting a zenith for entry that scales linearly for fakes but stays fixed for the honest. The verifier functions like a voyage across a map, rejecting any identity that lacks a unique, non-replayable solve. While one honest agent pays this base cost, an attacker managing 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a yarrow-like field of resistance. Any duplicate evidence triggers an identity burn.
